We need to find template that when applied to the molecule (the product) reproduces the reaction described: nucleophilic aromatic substitution where a nucleophile (amine) replaces a halide (likely F or Cl) on aromatic ring, with electron-withdrawing group (sulfonyl?). The provided precursors from previous step: ['CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1', 'O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F'].

So product is the combination of those two? Actually the product is the molecule given in input: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1S(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1F". That is the result of coupling the sulfonyl chloride? Wait the second precursor is O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F (aryl sulfonyl chloride with F). The first precursor is a tertiary amine with a phenyl? Actually the first has a heterocycle attached to aromatic ring with amine substituent. The product attaches the sulfonyl group to the amine? Actually product has ...N1CCN(... )CC1S(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1F. So the sulfonyl group attached to the nitrogen of the piperazine? The reaction is nucleophilic substitution of the sulfonyl chloride (Cl leaving) by the amine, forming sulfonamide. That's not SNAr but sulfonyl substitution. However the description mentions SNAr with halide leaving and amine nucleophile. But the product shows sulfonyl attached to aromatic ring with F still present. Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to aromatic ring with F still present, so the leaving group is Cl from sulfonyl chloride, not halide on aromatic. So functional groups broken: halide (Cl) formed: sulfonamide (amine). So functional_groups_broken: halide, functional_groups_formed: sulfonamide? But available groups include "sulfonamides". So we can search for functional_groups_broken ["halide"], functional_groups_formed ["sulfonamides"].
